text.arabic_uthmani: أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ وَتَأْتُونَ فِى نَادِيكُمُ ٱلْمُنكَرَ ۖ فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوا۟ ٱئْتِنَا بِعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ

words.gloss_range: rhetorical interrogative plus emphatic particle and 2mp suffix; the opening questions while treating the accusation as established
words.prose: {{ar:أَئِنَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:a-innakum}}) opens with a double pressure: the hamza questions, while the emphatic particle confirms the charge. The result is not neutral inquiry but incredulous accusation. Its bound plural suffix places the accused group inside the particle complex, and the opener scopes over the three coordinated accusations. Against 29:28, the inherited assertion is sharpened into a question-shaped rebuke.

topics.headline: question-form becomes accusatory rebuke
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens by questioning the addressees while already treating the charge as established.
topics.reason: The particle stack combines interrogative force with emphatic confirmation, and the discourse rows identify the opening as rebuke rather than information request.

topics.headline: single opener scopes over the tricolon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the first word frames all three following charges before any single act is named.
topics.reason: Scope and boundary evidence show the opening continues the prior emphatic frame from 29:28 while adding hamza-question force; the suffix binds the addressed group into that frame.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lam prefixed to the first verb, reinforcing the confirmed accusation inside the question frame
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) fixes certainty onto the first verb. Because it is prefixed to the action word inside the emphatic frame, the accusation begins as something pressed against resistant listeners, not as an open possibility.

topics.headline: lam fuses certainty to the first charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first accusation as confirmed against denial, not merely floated as a report.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as emphatic lam prefixed to the imperfect, and the rows connect it to the inna-lam confirmation frame continued from 29:28.

words.gloss_range: 2mp imperfect of coming/approaching, locally narrowed by its human object into charged approach and by repetition into a root thread
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers coming, arriving, bringing, and giving; local syntax selects approach here while preparing the later bring-demand
words.prose: {{ar:تَأْتُونَ}} ({{tr:taʾtūna}}) first names an ongoing collective practice. Its broad coming-root is narrowed by the direct object, so the motion image becomes charged approach toward men rather than ordinary arrival. The phrase also belongs to the recurring Lut accusation formula (7:81; 27:55), and in this local sequence it specifies the broader offense named in 29:28. The same root is planted for later reversal: it appears again in the third charge and then is turned back against Lut as the people’s imperative demand.

topics.headline: human object narrows coming into charged approach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb is narrowed by its direct human object into a habitual charged approach, not simple arrival.
topics.reason: QAC gives a 2mp imperfect with a direct accusative human object; attachment evidence confirms the object relation.

topics.headline: Lut accusation formula specifies the prior charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes this as a recurrent Lut accusation formula and as the concrete specification of the prior abstract offense.
topics.reason: The cited formula recurs at 7:81 and 27:55, and boundary rows connect this wording to the abstract charge in 29:28.

topics.headline: same root later returns as a counter-demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same root from accusation into the people’s later demand, where the direction is reversed.
topics.reason: Rows identify three occurrences of the same root in words 3, 9, and 21; the form shifts from imperfect accusation to imperative demand.

words.gloss_range: definite accusative plural object, naming men as the acted-upon class rather than a mere setting
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes male persons and foot/walking associations; local use selects adult males as definite object
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلرِّجَالَ}} ({{tr:al-rijāla}}) makes the first charge concrete. It is the definite accusative object, so the men are not the place among which the action happens; they are the acted-upon class. The root-image of footed movement is only a resonance, but beside the following road charge it gives the men-object a pedestrian trace before the ayah turns to route-cutting.

topics.headline: men are the definite acted-upon class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that men are grammatically the object category of the act, not a location or generic people.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the noun as definite accusative direct object; CRITICAL rows emphasize the male class and categorical force.

topics.headline: foot/walking image touches the route charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a local texture between the men-object and the following route-cutting charge, while the noun still means men.
topics.reason: The root-image row is useful as resonance because the next object is the way, but QAC keeps the local lexical sense as men, not walkers or feet.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction adding the second charge as equal-rank but cumulative
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the second accusation without making it subordinate. The list becomes cumulative: first charged approach, then route severance, then public reprehensible conduct.

topics.headline: waw adds an equal second charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second act as an independent charge in a cumulative indictment.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks coordination, and the rows show the conjunction opening the second member of the tricolon without subordination.

words.gloss_range: 2mp imperfect of cutting/severing, locally directed at the road/way as habitual obstruction
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers cutting, severing, and interruption; local Form I and object select road/way obstruction, not intensive dismemberment
words.prose: {{ar:تَقْطَعُونَ}} ({{tr:taqṭaʿūna}}) keeps the same habitual plural accusation and turns it toward continuity itself. With the road/way as object, cutting becomes the waylaying idiom of obstruction: the route that should remain open is severed. The Form I shape keeps the charge to simple severing or interruption; it does not ask the reader to imagine intensive dismemberment or a reciprocal break.

topics.headline: cutting makes route obstruction concrete
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels obstruction as a severing of continuity, not only as a general social wrong.
topics.reason: QAC gives a 2mp imperfect governing the definite way; root and idiom rows support cutting the road as obstruction/waylaying while also touching continuity themes.

topics.headline: Form I limits the image to interruption
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the action as one-sided interruption of a way, not intensive mutilation or reciprocal rupture.
topics.reason: Form evidence identifies simple Form I, not intensive Form II or reciprocal Form III.

words.gloss_range: definite singular accusative object: the road, route, or way whose continuity is cut
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes road, path, way, means, and divine-way usage; local phrase keeps physical route and moral-route pressure together
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّبِيلَ}} ({{tr:al-sabīla}}) is the thing cut. Its singular definiteness makes the route or way a recognized continuous corridor, not a vague backdrop. The phrase can carry the practical road-cutting sense while also keeping the moral way in view. That layered route-language matters because the same noun family often bears divine-way force. Within the surah, the route language continues when the way is barred (29:38) and sought by striving (29:69).

topics.headline: the way is the object whose continuity is attacked
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the way itself is attacked as a single recognized corridor, not merely used as scenery.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the noun as definite accusative direct object of the cutting verb, with singular definiteness supporting one salient route/way.

topics.headline: physical road and moral way remain live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the accusation carrying both road obstruction and moral-route obstruction without collapsing either side.
topics.reason: The sabīl semantic rows support road, way, means, and divine-route usage; local idiom licenses physical obstruction while Quranic usage keeps moral route pressure active.

topics.headline: same-surah route language continues later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can track this cut way into later same-surah obstruction and guidance language.
topics.reason: Rows cite later same-surah occurrences at 29:38 and 29:69, so references are kept as thread evidence without controlling the local parse.

words.gloss_range: second coordinating conjunction, opening the third charge while keeping it under the same accusation
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the third charge while keeping it under the first word’s accusatory scope. The repeated verb is visibly part of the same coordinated tricolon, and this second conjunction completes the three-part indictment.

topics.headline: second waw completes the tricolon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the third act as the culminating member of the same three-part accusation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks coordination, and the rows show this conjunction binding the repeated verb into the same tricolon under the opening question.

words.gloss_range: repeated 2mp imperfect, now reframed by a locative venue and moral object as public commission
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers coming, approaching, committing, and bringing; local complements shift this occurrence from human-object approach to committing a reprehensible act
words.prose: {{ar:تَأْتُونَ}} ({{tr:taʾtūna}}) repeats the earlier verb but not the earlier frame. Now a venue phrase and a moral object turn the root toward public commission of the reprehensible. By returning at the third member, the verb brackets the road-cutting charge and expands the indictment into a public venue with an explicit object of repudiated conduct.

topics.headline: same verb is reframed by venue and object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the identical verb changes force because its complements change.
topics.reason: QAC repeats the same imperfect form, while attachment evidence gives a locative phrase plus direct object for this occurrence.

topics.headline: repeated root brackets the public expansion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the tricolon expand from object relation to public venue and recognized social wrong.
topics.reason: Tricolon rows show the first and third charges bracket the middle charge; boundary evidence connects the previous broad offense to public repudiation here.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition governing the assembly as the venue containing the act
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) locates the act inside their assembly. The preposition does not make the venue a cause or instrument; it makes public containment part of the charge.

topics.headline: fī makes the offense public and located
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the wrong is staged inside a communal venue, not left private or abstract.
topics.reason: QAC marks a locative preposition, and attachment evidence makes it govern the following genitive venue as the location of the act.

words.gloss_range: genitive venue after the preposition, with 2mp possession marking their public assembly
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes calling, summoning, and assembly; local noun selects the concrete communal venue
words.prose: {{ar:نَادِيكُمُ}} ({{tr:nādīkumu}}) is not a neutral place marker. It is their assembly, with the suffix making the public venue grammatically belong to the accused group. Its calling-root resonance makes the place feel like a voiced forum, the kind of support base an assembly can be (96:17), while the local form remains the concrete venue.

topics.headline: their own assembly bears the offense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices collective responsibility: the venue is grammatically theirs.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as genitive after the preposition with a 2mp possessive suffix; rows emphasize communal ownership.

topics.headline: calling-root makes the venue socially audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the assembly as a voiced social forum or power base, while the local noun still means venue.
topics.reason: Root and occurrence rows support calling/summoning resonance and cite 96:17; local grammar selects a concrete gathering-place, not the act of calling.

words.gloss_range: definite accusative passive-participle noun: the recognized category of repudiated conduct they commit publicly
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers denial, unfamiliarity, refusal, and repudiation; local form selects what is morally refused or unrecognized
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُنكَرَ}} ({{tr:al-munkara}}) is the object they commit in the venue. The singular definite form classifies the act as a known category of repudiated conduct rather than vague badness. As a passive participle, it carries the sense of what is denied or refused recognition. The charge is that public practice has been made out of what the recognized order rejects. That role is marked: the same term later appears as what prayer prevents (29:45), while here it is what they actively bring into their assembly.

topics.headline: munkar is the committed object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reprehensible as a known category they actively commit, not a vague adjective for the gathering.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment mark the word as definite accusative object of the repeated verb; form rows emphasize singular category classification.

topics.headline: passive participle carries normative refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the moral term as what recognized order refuses, not merely as an intrinsic label.
topics.reason: The n-k-r rows tie the passive participle to denial, non-recognition, and contrast with recognized good; local use preserves this semantic pressure.

topics.headline: committed here, prevented later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can track the word from this public commission to later prevention language in the same surah.
topics.reason: Rows cite 29:45 and broader forbidding-munkar formulae; here the same category is unusually the thing committed, and boundary evidence links it to 29:28.

words.gloss_range: sequential/resumptive pivot from accusation to reported response
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the scene from direct accusation to narrated reply. It is both a narrative pivot and a sequence marker: the response follows directly from the confrontation.

topics.headline: fa pivots from charge to reply
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the answer arrive as an immediate narrative consequence of the accusation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks a result clause, and rows identify sequential plus resumptive force at the transition from direct address to narrated response.

words.gloss_range: negative particle beginning the negation-exception restriction of their only answer
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) begins the restriction. With the later exception particle, negation becomes onlyness: no answer remains for them except the quoted demand.

topics.headline: mā begins the only-answer restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that every possible answer is excluded except the defiant quote.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a negative particle, and the following exception particle turns the negation into a restriction formula.

words.gloss_range: perfect copular frame inside the restriction, treating the response as one completed answer unit
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers being, existing, becoming, and occurring; local use is a copular answer-frame, not a standalone existence claim
words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) frames the reply as a completed answer unit. Here it works as a copular narrative frame, not a separate claim about existence. Because it sits inside the restriction, the grammar foregrounds the answer slot before the actual speech arrives.

topics.headline: kāna frames one completed answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the quoted challenge treated as one completed response unit.
topics.reason: QAC marks perfect 3ms, and grammar rows make the answer noun the predicate in the standard construction.

topics.headline: answer slot is foregrounded before the quote
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the response category is foregrounded before the content is heard.
topics.reason: Rows identify the word’s role inside the only-answer formula and the thematic order that places answer before saying content.

words.gloss_range: accusative construct noun foregrounding the people's answer before the quoted content
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes answering and cutting/traversing imagery; local use selects answer while allowing the verbal incision image as resonance
words.prose: {{ar:جَوَابَ}} ({{tr:jawāba}}) makes answer itself the theme. As an accusative construct noun, it is specific through the following people-phrase and foregrounded before the content of their speech. The root image of cutting through remains useful as resonance: their answer cuts into the accusation, but perversely as a dare rather than compliance. The same response formula appears in other Lut tellings (7:82; 27:56) and earlier in this surah (29:24). The nominative case variant can make the answer the subject rather than the predicate, but the formula still funnels the people into one restricted answer.

topics.headline: answer is foregrounded and possessed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees answer itself made thematic before the quote, and owned by the people who give it.
topics.reason: QAC marks an accusative construct noun; rows show predicate function, construct definiteness, and nominal foregrounding.

topics.headline: answer cuts into the accusation as defiance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the reply as a verbal incision into Lut’s charge, while the local sense remains answer rather than compliance.
topics.reason: The root-image rows support cutting/traversing resonance, but the local noun means answer and does not imply favorable response.

topics.headline: formula recurs while case variation shifts syntax
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a repeated response formula whose case variants alter parse but not the restricted-defiance result.
topics.reason: Rows cite formula parallels at 7:82, 27:56, and 29:24; qiraat rows show accusative/nominative case variation without changing the only-answer content.

words.gloss_range: genitive construct dependent with 3ms suffix, assigning the answer to Lut's people in narrated frame
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes standing, rising, and people/community; local use selects the collective people with irony of standing against him
words.prose: {{ar:قَوْمِهِ}} ({{tr:qawmihī}}) shifts the accused audience into narrator language: they are his people, and their answer is assigned to them as a group. The standing-root resonance is ironic: the collective that should stand as a people is about to speak against him.

topics.headline: his people own the answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the addressed group re-presented as Lut’s people and as the source of the reply.
topics.reason: QAC marks a genitive construct dependent with 3ms suffix; rows show the shift from direct address to narrated ownership of the answer.

topics.headline: collective standing turns against him
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that the collective associated with standing together now stands against the prophet.
topics.reason: The root-image rows support standing/community resonance, while grammar shows a singular collective that later verbalizes as plural speakers.

words.gloss_range: exception particle completing the only-answer restriction
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) completes the restriction. It does not suspend the clause as unless; after the negation, it isolates the nominalized saying as the only answer left.

topics.headline: illā isolates the sole answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the saying-clause isolated as the only surviving response after negation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following nominalized saying as the exception; rows select exception/restriction rather than conditional unless.

words.gloss_range: maṣdariyya particle nominalizing their saying as the restricted answer-content
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) packages the act of saying as the restricted answer-content. The following quote is therefore both their direct speech and a nominalized speech-event inside the narrative verdict.

topics.headline: an turns saying into answer-content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the quote packaged as an answer-event inside the narrative frame before it is heard as direct speech.
topics.reason: QAC marks a subjunctive/maṣdariyya particle, and rows show it nominalizing the saying clause for the copular restriction.

words.gloss_range: 3mp perfect speech verb introducing the quoted challenge as completed collective utterance
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers saying and speech; local form frames the following imperative as their own direct speech act
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا}} ({{tr:qālū}}) turns the collective into plural speakers. The perfect form presents the speech act as delivered and complete. What it introduces is not a mere statement; the quoted speech performs a dare and moves toward a truth-test.

topics.headline: the collective answer is delivered as speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the singular people-phrase become plural speakers delivering a completed answer.
topics.reason: QAC marks perfect 3mp; rows emphasize completed speech and plural suffix resolving the collective source.

topics.headline: saying opens a performative challenge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what follows is not a report about belief but a spoken dare tied to truth-testing.
topics.reason: Rows identify direct speech whose first word is an imperative and whose close is the truth-class phrase; co-occurrence supports the speech/truth challenge field.

words.gloss_range: 2ms imperative with 1cp suffix, locally meaning bring us when governed by the following payload preposition
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers coming, arriving, bringing, and giving; local imperative plus payload selects bring and turns the earlier accusation root into a counter-demand
words.prose: {{ar:ٱئْتِنَا}} ({{tr:iʾtinā}}) reverses the address. The people who were accused as you-plural now command Lut as you-singular, and the attached us makes them the demanded recipients. With the following payload phrase, the root means bring rather than merely come. The command is a dare: deliver the punishment if the warning is true. This is the third occurrence of the same root in the ayah, but mood and address weaponize it: Lut’s accusation root becomes their counter-demand. The abrupt hamza cluster is phonetic pressure, while the demand itself creates the need for Lut’s next appeal (29:30).

topics.headline: imperative isolates Lut and targets us
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the discourse reverse from Lut accusing them-plural to them commanding Lut-singular.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2ms imperative with 1cp suffix; rows emphasize isolated addressee and demanded recipients.

topics.headline: payload construction turns come into bring
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the imperative as a defiant demand to deliver punishment, sharpened by the following condition.
topics.reason: The following prepositional payload selects the bring sense, and the conditional phrase makes the command pragmatically a truth-test dare.

topics.headline: accusation root becomes counter-demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same root from Lut’s charge into the people’s weaponized counter-demand and forward into 29:30.
topics.reason: Rows connect word 21 to earlier same-root forms and to the next speech in 29:30; variant rows affect phonetic entry, not command morphology.

words.gloss_range: preposition that supplies the carried payload of the imperative
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is the small word that supplies the payload. It governs the punishment phrase, turning the imperative into bring us with this specified consequence.

topics.headline: bi supplies the carried punishment payload
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the preposition is semantically essential: it makes the command mean bring with a specified payload.
topics.reason: QAC marks a preposition governing the punishment noun; rows show it scopes over the divine-punishment phrase and activates the bring-with construction.

words.gloss_range: construct noun governed by the preposition and bound to the divine name as demanded punishment
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes punishment and a sweetness/freshness branch; local sense is punishment, with deprivation irony as narrowed resonance
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابِ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābi}}) packages punishment as the payload they dare Lut to bring. In construct with the divine name, it is not human retaliation but punishment sourced from God. The root-family contrast with sweetness or freshness survives as narrowed irony: what they demand is punishment, a deprivation of what sustains. That demand is not left hanging: punishment language returns later as the very thing whose coming is warned (29:53; 29:54), and the next narrative movement specifies the consequence they invoke.

topics.headline: punishment is bound to God and made bringable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the demanded punishment is specifically divine and packaged as the object-like payload of their dare.
topics.reason: QAC marks a genitive construct noun after the preposition; rows emphasize construct definiteness and divine attribution.

topics.headline: punishment carries deprivation irony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses punishment as deprivation and loss of sweetness, while the local meaning remains punishment.
topics.reason: Root evidence supports withholding and sweetness/freshness branches, but local syntax and construct select punishment as the active sense.

topics.headline: demanded punishment returns later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the demanded punishment into later same-surah warning and narrative consequence.
topics.reason: Rows cite demand formula parallels including 8:32 and 29:53, plus later same-surah return at 29:53 and 29:54 and narrative specification after this verse.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in genitive construct, specifying the punishment's source
words.root_gloss_range: root discussions include worship and divine-name derivation; local use is the proper divine name as genitive source
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) seals the punishment phrase with the divine name. Their dare therefore exceeds a challenge to Lut and invokes the very source of punishment. The derivational background is only resonance, but the local paradox is clear: their defiance invokes the divine authority before turning to the truth-test.

topics.headline: divine name specifies the punishment source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the dare escalate beyond Lut personally to the divine source named in the construct.
topics.reason: QAC marks the proper divine name as genitive dependent of the punishment construct; rows emphasize source and recognizable divine-punishment pairing.

topics.headline: they invoke the authority they challenge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paradox that their defiance speaks the divine name before testing truthfulness.
topics.reason: Derivational-dispute rows are kept as resonance, while local grammar fixes the proper name as genitive source; the phrase lands on the name before the condition begins.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle of doubtful testing rather than expected concession
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) makes the command conditional in a skeptical way. It tests the premise instead of granting that Lut’s truthfulness is expected. Its answer is supplied by the preceding imperative: if the condition holds, bring it. That ellipsis tightens the demand into a dare.

topics.headline: conditional particle encodes doubt
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears their condition as a skeptical test, not a concession that Lut is likely truthful.
topics.reason: Rows contrast this conditional particle with an expectation particle; QAC marks it as conditional governing the following verb.

topics.headline: the implied answer points back to the imperative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior command silently serving as the condition’s proof-action: if truthful, bring it.
topics.reason: Rows identify the conditional answer as supplied by the preceding imperative, making the command a compressed truth-test dare.

words.gloss_range: 2ms perfect inside a condition, testing present status rather than simple past existence
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers being, existing, becoming, and occurring; local conditional use tests Lut's truth-status
words.prose: {{ar:كُنتَ}} ({{tr:kunta}}) is formally perfect, but inside the condition it tests status: if you are. The question is not past existence but present standing in the truth-class. The singular ending sustains the reversal of address: the group challenges Lut alone, and the clause closes the quote on his truth-status.

topics.headline: past form tests present truth-status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the form as conditional status-testing, not a question about whether Lut was truthful in the past.
topics.reason: Rows note perfect morphology under a condition, where the local phrase tests present class-status before the truth-class complement.

topics.headline: singular address keeps Lut isolated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the group’s reply isolate Lut personally and close on his truth-status.
topics.reason: QAC marks 2ms morphology; rows connect this singular address to the imperative and to the closing conditional clause.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking membership in the truth-bearing class
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) makes the predicate a membership test. Lut is challenged as being from among the truthful, not merely described by a loose adjective.

topics.headline: min makes truthfulness a class membership test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the challenge asks whether Lut belongs among recognized truthful ones, not whether he can attach a bare adjective to himself.
topics.reason: QAC marks a preposition governing the following genitive plural; rows identify partitive/class-membership force.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive masculine plural active participle: the recognized class of truthful ones
words.root_gloss_range: root range covers truth, confirmation, charity, friendship, and dowry through verified commitment; local form selects persons characterized by truthfulness
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ṣādiqīna}}) names the recognized class of truth-bearers. As an active participle plural, it tests durable truthful character, not whether one statement happens to work. The ayah therefore lands not on punishment itself but on the truth-test formula, a challenge pattern also cited at 6:143 and 11:32. The wider root family adds narrowed pressure of verified commitment, and the same root recalls the surah’s earlier truth-testing theme (29:3).

topics.headline: definite participle names truth-bearers as a class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the final phrase tests durable character in a recognized class of truth-bearers.
topics.reason: QAC marks a definite genitive masculine plural active participle after the preposition; rows emphasize class, human plural form, and durable truth-trait.

topics.headline: the ayah lands on a challenge formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah end not on punishment itself but on a formulaic truth-test dare.
topics.reason: Rows identify the closing truth phrase as the evaluative hinge and cite challenge-formula parallels at 6:143 and 11:32.

topics.headline: root family links truth to verified commitment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the closing truth word with verified commitment and the surah’s earlier truth-testing theme.
topics.reason: The broad root family is narrowed to resonance because the local form selects truthful persons; the same root appears in the surah’s trial theme at 29:3.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: تأتون الرجال / تقطعون السبيل / تأتون في ناديكم المنكر
baseline_models.mechanism: The coordinated clauses form one civic access-system: men are approached, a traversable route is forcibly stopped, and a gathered venue converts reprehensible conduct into group practice. Movement toward bodies, control of shared space, and public reinforcement work together.

activation_trace.role: Literal coming or approach supplies the repeated ingress that links the bodily and assembly clauses.
The male-person branch identifies the human targets around which the first access relation is organized.
Road-cutting by seizure or obstruction makes spatial coercion, not mere interruption, the middle mechanism.
The extended traversable road supplies the shared channel over which the group exercises control.
The gathering in a club or council supplies the public institution that hosts and reinforces the conduct.
The ugly act that should be checked marks what the assembly instead makes performable.

changed_reading.before: Three adjacent but separable offenses: approaching men, highway robbery, and bad behavior in a club.
changed_reading.after: One public regime of coercive access: vulnerable bodies, shared routes, and the assembly that authorizes the conduct form a single mechanism.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين
baseline_models.mechanism: The restrictive answer formula empties the reply-slot and replaces argument with an imperative. Bringing punishment becomes the demanded realization by which Lot's truthfulness is to be measured.

activation_trace.role: A verbal reply supplies the expected discourse-slot that the restrictive construction reduces to one command.
Uttered speech supplies the group's actual response, whose content refuses the accusations rather than answering them.
Bringing or delivering gives the imperative its demanded event: punishment must be produced before them.
Painful punishment supplies the proposed empirical verdict.
Truth realized through fulfillment or action turns veracity from a spoken claim into a demanded occurrence.

changed_reading.before: The people deny Lot and mockingly ask for punishment.
changed_reading.after: They refuse discursive answer and impose an event-test: only immediate punitive realization will count as truth.

baseline_models.mechanism: One root stages two accused approaches and the counter-command to bring something back. Agency turns within the ayah: they come toward men and into the assembly with wrong, then order punitive arrival toward themselves.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah opens by treating professed claims as material put to assay and by distinguishing those whose truth is enacted. It also shows a person equating human affliction with divine punishment. Against that frame, the focus challenge is a corrupted testing protocol: the accused community tries to control the proof condition by demanding pain now.

activation_trace.role: Truth verified in fulfillment anchors the focus demand for an enacted rather than merely verbal proof.

Affliction as trial supplies the pressure that a person can misclassify as final punishment.
Punitive pain supplies the verdict-category with which human trial is wrongly equated.

structural_cues: 29:2-3 moves from saying 'we believe' through testing to the disclosure of truthful and lying claimants.
29:10 explicitly compares human affliction with God's punishment, exposing confusion between pressure and verdict.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies claim, assay, enacted truth, and a trial/punishment confusion; I infer that the group seizes those categories to dictate an immediate proof-test. A live alternative is that their words are ordinary mockery without a deliberate testing logic.

changed_reading.before: If you are truthful is a generic skeptical formula.
changed_reading.after: The formula attempts to commandeer the surah's assay of truth by making immediate pain the only admissible evidence.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the surah, a path can recruit people under false liability, be obstructed despite clear sight, stand outside or inside protected space, and become the object of divine guidance. The focus road-cutting therefore remains literal predation while also functioning as anti-guidance: the group controls who can move, where they can move, and which course can be followed.

activation_trace.role: Seizing or blocking road-users anchors the model in concrete route predation.
A traversable route supplies the channel whose physical and directive availability is cut.
The offered 'our path' supplies a socially recruited route that can misdirect rather than merely transport.

The traveled path becomes a course from which even sighted people can be diverted.
A spatial sanctuary supplies the protected-zone contrast to the focus community's control of exposed routes.
Swift snatching supplies the embodied danger faced by people outside protected circulation.
Gentle direction toward road and truth supplies the positive inverse of coercive route control.
The closing plural paths widen the focus road into a surah-spanning network of possible courses.

structural_cues: 29:12 offers 'our path' with a false promise to carry another's liability, while 29:38 depicts diversion from the path despite sight.
29:67 contrasts a protected precinct with people snatched around it, and 29:69 closes with divinely guided paths.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies literal routes, recruited courses, diversion, protected space, snatching, and guidance; I infer that physical road predation instantiates a broader monopoly over access and direction. The materially live alternative is that تقطعون السبيل is only literal highway obstruction while the other path uses remain thematic echoes.

changed_reading.before: They rob or obstruct travelers on a road.
changed_reading.after: Their literal route predation is the spatial face of anti-guidance: a civic power that captures travelers and constrains available courses.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exact restrictive response formula already occurred in 29:24, where Abraham's people replace answer with commands to kill or burn him. Its reuse in the focus makes the demand for punishment another collective anti-answer: prophetic speech is met by forcing discourse toward annihilation or catastrophic adjudication.

activation_trace.role: Verbal response anchors the repeated formula's ostensibly dialogical slot.

Putting to death supplies one earlier way the collective converts reply into elimination.
Fire and flame supply the alternative command by which argument is displaced into destructive force.

structural_cues: 29:24 and 29:29 share the sequence فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا almost verbatim.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact formulaic repetition plus commands to kill, burn, or bring punishment; I infer a shared collective response-grammar that terminates dialogue through force. A live alternative is that the repetition is only narrative parallelism without a functional theory of anti-answer.

changed_reading.before: The punishment request is a locally improvised taunt.
changed_reading.after: It belongs to a repeated collective anti-answer in which proclamation is met by redirecting speech toward annihilation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The club is activated as social infrastructure rather than incidental scenery. Worldly mutual affection can bind a group around false objects, Lot names his people as active corrupters, and the surah's alliance-house is structurally weak. The nadi produces public reinforcement for wrong while disguising the fragility of that solidarity.

activation_trace.role: The assembled club supplies the concrete social institution in which conduct becomes mutually visible and repeatable.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an assembly, group affection, corruption, and a weak alliance-house; I supply the arrow that the nadi manufactures solidarity around the act. The live alternative is that the club is only a venue and the alliance material concerns unrelated communities.

changed_reading.before: Wrong happens in a pre-existing social club.
changed_reading.after: The club is a group technology that displays, normalizes, and protects wrong, even though the solidarity it creates is structurally brittle.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding ayah names the فاحشة, the focus locates المنكر in an assembly, and 29:45 recombines الفحشاء والمنكر as what established prayer restrains. This gives the focus a counter-practice: the nadi is a formative gathering that rehearses transgression, while prayer and remembrance form inhibition.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lexical recombination and an explicit restraint relation; I infer that club-performance and prayer are rival formative practices. A live alternative is that 29:45 states a general moral scope without specifically answering the nadi.

context_deltas.mechanism: The command to bring punishment is followed by messengers announcing destruction, then generalized later as hastening punishment. The later sequence answers the group's temporal premise: arrival has an appointed timing, occurs suddenly, already encompasses its objects, and becomes something experienced rather than observed as a proof-token.

structural_cues: 29:31-34 follows the challenge with messengers' arrival, announced destruction, and a punishment descending on the town.
29:53-55 repeats hastening punishment, then moves through appointed delay, sudden arrival, enclosure, and 'taste what you used to do.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate narrative sequence and later lexical recurrence; I infer that both retrospectively answer the focus demand by reversing its temporal and epistemic terms. A live alternative is that 29:31-34 alone fulfills the local request while 29:53-55 addresses different challengers without deliberate echo.

changed_reading.before: Bring us punishment is a hyperbolic dare whose force ends with the conversation.
changed_reading.after: The dare enters a surah-long haste motif: punishment comes on its own timing, encloses the challengers, and changes demanded evidence into experienced consequence.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The echo is surprising because رِجَال in the focus and أَرْجُل in 29:55 occupy different semantic branches of one root. It remains anchored in the focus's ر ج ل occurrence and gains a bodily reversal from punishment arriving beneath their feet, but downstream prose should present it only as a root-level rhetorical resonance, never as lexical equivalence or translation.

activation_trace.role: The male-person branch supplies the people approached in the focus accusation.
The bodily feet branch relocates the shared root to the actors' own footing under enveloping punishment.
Experiencing or undergoing supplies the reversal from acting upon others to bodily consequence.

changed_reading.before: الرجال identifies only the human objects of the first accusation.
changed_reading.after: A contained whole-surah root echo moves from the men approached to punishment beneath the actors' feet, turning bodily agency back upon them.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading is branch-distant because جواب ordinarily functions here as verbal answer, while the same root inventory also images a penetrating cut or breach. It remains anchored in جواب, the focus's explicit cutting, and the violent 29:24 response parallel; downstream prose should qualify it as an 'as if' material image of discourse rupturing into force, not an alternative lexical gloss.

activation_trace.role: A penetrating cut or breach supplies the exploratory material image for what this answer does to dialogue.
The ordinary verbal-response branch keeps the image anchored to the actual construction.
Severing and separation provide an internal material analogue for the reply's termination of exchange.
The earlier formula's command to kill shows the repeated answer-slot opening directly into destructive force.

changed_reading.before: Their answer merely fails to address Lot's accusation.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material image, the 'answer' breaches the space of dialogue and lets coercive force replace exchange.

strongest_changes: The exact 29:24 response formula turns the focus challenge into a repeated collective anti-answer rather than an isolated taunt.
The surah's path network expands literal road predation into a civic mechanism of captured movement and anti-guidance.
The 29:45 recombination of الفحشاء والمنكر supplies prayer and remembrance as the counter-practice to assembly-normalized wrong.
The 29:53-55 haste sequence reverses demanded proof into sudden, encompassing, experienced consequence.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah recurrence made the focus less a catalog of offenses than a coupled system of bodily access, route control, public reinforcement, and coercive proof. Repeated path, answer, restraint, and arrival language turns both the group's conduct and its challenge back upon it.
remaining_uncertainties: The anti-guidance layer of تقطعون السبيل may be thematic superposition over a primarily literal road-predation sense.
Treating the nadi as a solidarity-producing institution is mechanistically coherent but more inferential than reading it as a venue.
The men/feet and answer/breach outliers are rhetorical branch echoes and should not be promoted to lexical claims.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The severed way as public infrastructure.** ق ط ع B023 is explicitly road robbery or blocking the way; B001 is cutting off. Coming to men, cutting the path, and public wrongdoing in the assembly form a social-spatial sequence. I infer that the conduct makes passage unsafe and normalizes obstruction communally; “cutting the way” reads as destruction of shared access, not only an isolated act.
2. **Severance of connection.** ق ط ع B007 is severance of relationship or connection. The same sequence can be read relationally: acts in the public gathering rupture the bonds by which a community remains traversable and answerable. This is a distinct mechanism from literal road-blocking, and the later demand for punishment displays the completed break with corrective speech.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 29:38 shows people being blocked from the path despite sight, while 29:69 ends by opening plural paths to strivers. The cut way here becomes one pole of a surah-wide contest over traversability.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Corruption captures both movement infrastructure and public assembly.** Lexical evidence: `تَقْطَعُون`, root `ق ط ع`, `B023` (road robbery or blocking the way) with `B007` (severance of connection); `ٱلسَّبِيل`, root `س ب ل`, `B001` (extended traversed way); `نَادِيكُم`, root `ن د و`, `B001` (gathering in a council); and `ٱلْمُنكَر`, root `ن ك ر`, `B006` (the condemned thing corrected or rebuked). Structural cue: private-directed approach, road cutting, and council conduct are listed as one mechanism before the community answers collectively. Assigned role: road and council are the channels through which a society moves and recognizes norms; cutting and condemned conduct disable both. Abductive move: I infer that these are not three random charges but a system in which transgression occupies bodies, routes, and assembly. Reading change: the ayah diagnoses public-order corruption, not only private conduct.

2. **The response redirects the accused “coming” into a dare that punishment come.** Lexical evidence: repeated `تَأْتُون / تَأْتُون / ٱئْتِنَا`, root `ء ت ي`, `B001` (coming and arriving); `جَوَاب`, root `ج و ب`, `B003` (answer) with activated `B001` (cutting through); and `ٱلصَّادِقِين`, root `ص د ق`, `B004` (confirmation and fulfillment). Structural cue: after two accusations built on “you come,” their sole answer is “bring us” punishment, making fulfillment the test of truth. Assigned role: the imperative attempts to seize control of arrival-time and convert warning into spectacle. Abductive move: the packet supplies the lexical reversal; I infer that the dare avoids the charges by demanding an external event rather than repairing the cut social channels. Reading change: their answer is another severance of dialogue, now disguised as an empirical challenge.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: - **Later activation (`29:38`, `29:69`):** One people are turned from `ٱلسَّبِيل` despite insight, while the close opens `سُبُلَنَا` through guidance. The cut road in `29:29` thus belongs to a surah-wide path mechanism: corruption blocks public passage, captured valuation diverts it, and striving receives reopened routes.

baseline.text: Siz erkeklere yaklaşıyor, yolu kesiyor ve toplantınızda kötülük yapıyorsunuz, öyle mi? Halkının tek cevabı, "Doğru söylüyorsan Allah'ın azabını bize getir!" demek oldu.

findings.text: Yol kesme ile toplantıdaki kötülük birlikte, kişisel eylemin ötesinde geçişi ve kamusal düzeni işlemez hale getiren bir toplumsal altyapı bozulmasıdır.
Yolun kesilmesi ilişkisel olarak da topluluğun bağlarını koparır; azabı istemeleri, düzeltici sözle kalan bağlantıyı da reddeder.
Suçlamadaki “yaklaşma” sözünü “azabı getir” diye geri çevirmeleri, asıl suçlamaya cevap vermek yerine geliş zamanını denetleyecekleri bir gösteri talep eder.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Cutting the Worked Road
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Travelers move on a known track toward resources until an obstacle, seizure, or exhausted means interrupts passage.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: crossing a distance or water `quranic:root_001240:B003/m01`; a stranded traveler whose means fail `quranic:root_001240:B006/m01`; highway seizure and obstruction `quranic:root_001240:B023/m01`; an extended traversable road `quranic:root_000672:B001/m01`; road users and travelers `quranic:root_000672:B002/m01`; preventing and turning away `quranic:root_000848:B001/m01`; a route leading to water `quranic:root_000848:B004/m01`; a worked road `quranic:root_001046:B011/m01`; walkers on foot `quranic:root_000546:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Cutting the road is a full disruption of public mobility: a known worked track and its resource route are blocked until the traveler becomes "cut off" through lost mount, food, or money. The lexical assembly makes obstruction an attack on the infrastructure that lets strangers continue.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The forum is not a neutral venue but an amplifier: gathering, raised voice, circulating talk, and shame-producing language create the social force of the act. identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi dalın çekirdeğini gelme ve ulaşma olarak doğrular; kolaylık niteliği açıklamalardan yalnız birinde belirgindir. Gelmeyi isteme ise dalın genel anlamı değil, ayrı bir kalıpta görülen kullanımdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynakların tümü, yağmurun düştüğü başka bir yerden yağmur almamış bölgeye ulaşan seli veya kendi yatağında dışarıdan geçip gelen seli tanımlar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnız dışarıdaki yağış alanından gelen sel kalıbına bağlıdır; genel sel veya genel akış değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız belirtilen sel nitelemesine bağlı tutulur ve sözcükten genel bir yalın anlam türetilmez.

concept_map.definition: Yağmur alan başka bir bölgeden, yağmur almamış bir bölgeye yatağı boyunca ulaşıp geçen seldir.

facets.statement: Selin suyu yağmur alan başka bir bölgeden gelir.
Sel, kendi yağmurunu almamış bir bölgeye ulaşıp oradan geçer.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, yerel yağıştan doğmayan ve yağmur alan başka bir yerden geçerek gelen sel sınırında birleşir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Selin ulaştığı yerde yağmur yağmamış, su başka bir yağış alanından gelmişse kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Selin dışarıdaki yağış alanından gelmesi koşulunu korur.

error_profile.adds: Yerel yağmurdan doğan selleri de kapsayarak zorunlu dış kaynak koşulunu kaldırır.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal her türlü su akışını, akıtmayı, akan suyu ve akış yerini kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da yatakta ilerleyen akan su bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal kaynağı ve hedef bölgenin yağış durumuyla sınırlı özel bir sel türüdür; komşu dal genel akış alanıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; genel su akışı dalı, bu kalıbın dışarıdan gelme koşulunu en açık biçimde gösterdi.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, içinde bulunduğu topluluğa mensup olmayan yabancı erkeği ortak biçimde tanımlar ve dal çerçevesindeki sınırı doğrular.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu anlam yalnız bir topluluk içinde onlardan olmayan yabancı kişi nitelemesine bağlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım kişi niteleyen kalıpla sınırlıdır; her gelen kişi veya dışarıdan gelen sel bu kapsama alınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir topluluk içinde bulunan, fakat o topluluğa mensup olmayan yabancı erkektir.

facets.statement: Kişi bir topluluğun içinde bulunur ancak o topluluktan değildir.
Kişi topluluğa göre yabancı ve dışarıdan gelmiş sayılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, kişinin bulunduğu topluluğa mensup olmaması ve bu nedenle yabancı sayılması üzerinde birleşir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir kişinin içinde bulunduğu topluluğun mensubu olmadığını belirtmek için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Topluluk içinde bulunma ve ona mensup olmama sınırını korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: içinde bulunduğu topluluğa mensup olmayan yabancı adam

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin gruba göre dışarıdan oluşunu korur.
error_profile.adds: Bir topluluk içinde bulunmayan kişiler ile tanınmayan şeyleri de kapsayabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kişinin topluluğa yabancı oluşunu bildirir, sonradan karışma biçimini zorunlu kılmaz.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal topluluğa dışarıdan girip ona karışan kişi görünümünü özellikle taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal bir topluluk içinde o topluluktan olmayan kişiyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal mensubiyet dışılığını merkez alır; komşu dal dışarıdan girme ve topluluğa karışma görünümünü daha belirgin taşır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; topluluğa karışmış yabancı dalı mensubiyet ile sonradan giriş arasındaki farkı en iyi gösterdi.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ekin ve hurmanın ürünü, gelişmesi ve bol verimi ile suyun çoğalmasını destekler. Çalkalanan tulumdan yağın çıkması ise yalnız ayrı kalıbın kaynak ifadesiyle açıklanabilen, çekirdeğe bağlı olmayan bir kullanımdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bitkisel ürün ve artış çekirdektir; suyun çoğalması uzantı, tulumdan yağ çıkması ise ayrı kalıp kullanımıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Ürün ve gelişme bildiren biçim, suyun çoğalması ve çalkalanan tulumda yağın belirmesini bildiren kalıptan ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Ekin ve hurmanın gelişip ürün vermesi, ürününün ve veriminin bol olmasıdır; suyun çoğalması da bu artış alanına uzanır. Ayrı bir kalıp, çalkalanan tulumda yağın ortaya çıkmasını bildirir.

facets.statement: Ekin veya hurma gelişir, ürün verir ve verimi artar.
Suyun miktarı çoğalır.
Ayrı bir kalıpta çalkalanan tulumun yağı ortaya çıkar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt bitkisel gelişme, ürün ve bol verimi merkez alır; su artışı ve tulum yağının belirmesi farklı kapsamlı kullanımlardır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Ekin veya hurmanın gelişmesi, ürün çıkarması ve veriminin artması birlikte anlatılacağında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bitkisel gelişme, ürün ve bolluk çekirdeğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Ekinin veya hurmanın çıkan ürünü ve yüksek verimi adlandırıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bitkinin ürünü ile verim bolluğunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Gelişme sürecini, suyun çoğalmasını ve tulum yağı kullanımını dışarıda bırakır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: ekin ve hurmanın gelişmesi, ürünü ve bol verimi

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal ürünün yanında gelişme, verim bolluğu ve suyun çoğalması kapsamlarını taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal ağaç, hurma, ekin ve toprağın verdiği ürünü daha genel bir ürün adı olarak kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal ekin ve hurmanın meydana getirdiği ürünü anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal ürünle birlikte gelişme ve bolluk sürecini öne çıkarır; komşu dal ürünün kendisine daha genel biçimde yönelir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; ürün dalı, ürünün kendisi ile gelişme ve bol verim arasındaki ayrımı en iyi belirginleştirdi.
branches.what_is_ar: ريع الزرع والنخل وثمرهما، وكثرة الماء، وما يجيء من زبد السقاء عند الصحاح والمفردات

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yönetime ödenen vergi veya baş vergisini ortak alan olarak verir ve aynı toplu iddia içinde bir kişiye sunulan rüşvet kullanımını da bildirir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Düzenli veya zorunlu kamu ödemesi çekirdektir; rüşvet, aynı biçimin ayrı kalıptaki özel kullanımıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Vergi adı olarak kullanılan biçim ile birine rüşvet vermeyi bildiren kalıp kapsam bakımından ayrılır.

concept_map.definition: Bir topluluğun veya kişinin yönetime ödediği vergi ya da baş vergisidir. Ayrı bir kalıpta, bir kimseye çıkar sağlamak için verilen rüşveti veya rüşvet verme eylemini anlatır.

facets.statement: Topluluk veya kişi yönetime vergi niteliğinde para öder.
Ödeme baş vergisi veya benzeri yükümlülük niteliği taşır.
Ayrı bir kullanımda bir kimseye rüşvet verilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu iddia vergi ve baş vergisi anlamlarını ortaklaştırır; rüşvet kullanımı kaynaklara ayrı ayrı dağıtılamayan özel bir karşılık olarak aynı iddiada yer alır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yönetime ödenen mali yükümlülük ile ayrı rüşvet kullanımı birlikte gösterileceğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Vergi, baş vergisi ve ayrı rüşvet kullanımını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Topluluğun veya kişinin yönetime yaptığı zorunlu mali ödeme söz konusu olduğunda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yönetime yapılan mali yükümlülük ödemesini korur.
error_profile.loses: Rüşvet olarak verilen ödeme kullanımını dışarıda bırakır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal aynı biçimin rüşvet kullanımını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal kişiye, köleye veya toprağa konan vergi, gelir ve görev ödemelerini daha geniş sınıflar halinde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal bir kişi veya topluluğa yüklenen vergi ve kamu ödemesi alanında kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal vergi adının yanında rüşvet kullanımına sahiptir; komşu dal ise üzerine konan mali yükümlülük türlerini daha geniş kapsar.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; mali yükümlülük komşusu vergi çekirdeği ile rüşvet uzantısı arasındaki sınırı en iyi gösterdi.

facets.statement: Deve yürüyüş sırasında ön ayaklarını geri getirir.
Bu hareket devenin yürüyüş niteliği olarak değerlendirilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, devenin yürüyüşünde ön ayakların geri getirilişini aynı hareket niteliği olarak tanımlar.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal yürüyen bir hayvanın ayaklarını geri getirme hareketini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal deve ve ön ayaklarla sınırlıdır; komşu dal hayvan ve yürüyüş türü bakımından daha geniştir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yarışın son sınırı, işlek ya da yürünmüş yol, yol kavşağı ve bir evin karşısında veya hizasında olma kullanımlarını açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Yol adı, yarış sonu ve konumsal hizalama aynı biçim ailesindeki ayrı kullanımlardır; biri ötekine indirgenmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yol ve son sınır bildiren adlar ile bir evin karşısında bulunmayı bildiren kalıp ayrı kapsamlar olarak korunur.

concept_map.definition: İşlek veya yürünmüş ana yol, yolların birleştiği yer ya da yarış atlarının koşusunun bittiği son sınırdır. Bir konum kalıbında, bir evin karşısında veya onunla aynı hizada bulunmayı bildirir.

facets.statement: İnsanların kullandığı işlek veya yürünmüş ana yol adlandırılır.
Yolların birleştiği kavşak veya yolun belirgin ana kesimi anlatılır.
Yarış atlarının koşusunun ulaştığı son sınır adlandırılır.
Bir yapı başka bir yapının karşısında veya aynı hizasında bulunur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt yol, kavşak ve yarış sonu anlamlarını; ayrıca yapıların karşı karşıya veya aynı hizada oluşunu bildiren kalıbı bir araya getirir.

concept_gloss.text: işlek ana yol, son sınır ve karşı hizası
concept_gloss.applicability: Yol ailesindeki temel adlar ile yarış sonu ve karşıda bulunma kullanımları topluca temsil edileceğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yol, kavşak, yarış sonu ve konumsal hizalama kapsamlarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İnsanların yürüdüğü veya yolların birleştiği belirgin yol adlandırıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İşlek ve yürünmüş yol anlamını korur.
error_profile.loses: Yarış sonu ile bir yapının karşısında veya hizasında bulunma kullanımlarını dışarıda bırakır.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yolun toplandığı ana cadde ve bu caddeyi tutma eylemiyle sınırlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal işlek ana yol ve yolların birleştiği yer anlamında kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal yol çekirdeğinin ötesinde yarış sonu ve konumsal hizalama kullanımlarına sahiptir; komşu dal bu uzantıları taşımaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; ana yol ve kavşak komşusu, dalın yol dışındaki yarış sonu ve hizalama kapsamlarını en iyi açığa çıkardı.
branches.what_is_ar: الميتاء والميداء: آخر الغاية، والطريق العامر أو المسلوك، ومجتمع الطريق، ومحاذاة الدار

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli kalıplarda kişiye ölüm, ağır hastalık, bela veya kırık gelmesini; malın yok olmasını; kişinin öldürülüp götürülmesini ve düşmanın yaklaşmasını destekler. Genel olarak gelişin iyi veya kötü olabileceği notu, bu dalın yalnız zararlı kalıplarını genişletmez.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnız belirtilen zarar ve tehdit kalıplarına bağlıdır; genel gelme eylemi veya her türlü yok oluş değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Ölüm, hastalık, mal kaybı, yenilgi ve düşman yaklaşması anlamları yalnız kendi kalıplarında korunur.

concept_map.definition: Belirli kalıplarda bir kişiye ölüm, ağır hastalık, bela veya kırık gelmesi; malının yok olması; öldürülüp götürülmesi ya da düşmanın ona yaklaşmasıdır.

facets.statement: Kişi ölüm, ağır hastalık, bela veya uzuv kırılması gibi ağır bir zarara uğrar.
Bir kişinin malı yok olur.
Bir kişi öldürülür, götürülür veya üzerinde üstünlük kurulur.
